plan.title: Entropy: Why Everything Spreads Out
plan.description: Entropy measures how evenly energy is spread out in a system. The second law of thermodynamics says isolated systems drift toward higher entropy, which is why some processes can never be reversed.

beats.narration: Why can't you unscramble an egg? The answer is entropy, a measure of how spread out energy is.

props.text: Why can't you unscramble an egg?

beats.narration: Low entropy means energy is concentrated in one place. High entropy means it is spread out evenly. Hot coffee cools because its heat disperses.
The second law says an isolated system never loses entropy. That is why some processes are irreversible. Nature drifts toward spread-out.

props.text: Isolated systems drift toward higher entropy.
